set.descent_text: Both finishes end on the Notch Spire, directly above the descent. From the notch, the standard descent is the West Gully, a third- to fourth-class talus gully reached by working north and uphill along a cairned, well-worn path from the spire; cliffs lie below that path, so stay on it. Snow can linger in the upper gully until midsummer, and the exposed traverse is a poor place in an electrical storm. Rappelling the west face from bolted stations near the notch is the other choice and takes two 60 m ropes for about three rappels. At the foot of the gully, retrace the approach past Lake Helene to Bear Lake.
set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the Fern Lake trail for roughly 3 miles to the saddle between Joe Mills Mountain and Notchtop. An unsigned but obvious trail on the left drops to Lake Helene. Circle the lake counterclockwise, then follow the braided trail uphill through a gully that can hold snow until midsummer, watching for cairns, to a small tarn at the foot of the south ridge. The Direct South Ridge starts a short way past the southeast corner of the mountain: find a ramp that cuts back to the right and follow it to the base. The first two or three pitches are easy fifth class.

review.notes: Route page: start and top-out; Spiral Route, Topnotch, AAI and trip pages: West Gully and three-rappel descents; NPS and route pages agree on roughly 3 miles to Lake Helene.

set.descent_text: The route finishes at the notch and on the top of the tower and south ridge. As the name suggests, it is also the rappel route: the bolted anchors take two ropes, and the top anchor sits near the top of the Notch Spire. Coming from the true summit, a ramp heading down from the notch reaches a lower top anchor, which also keeps the rope from dragging across a loose ledge. The other option is the West Gully, a fourth-class scramble, then retrace the approach past Lake Helene to Bear Lake.

Instant Clarification is on the west face, above the old descent gully. It begins off the grassy ledge where the South Ridge route starts, just right of the gully that drops from the notch, in a groove that leads to a bolt about 25 feet up.

review.notes: Route page: location and finish; trip page: two-rope rappels, West Gully alternative, anchors.

The Spiral Route is on the left wall, Relief Train is front and center, and Mornin' is the crack to its right.

review.notes: Route page: location relative to Spiral and Mornin, notch alignment; descent facts from Spiral Route, AAI and trip page.

set.descent_text: The ninth pitch ends on the summit of the Notch Spire. Drop back to the notch, then use the standard descent. Circle the lake counterclockwise, then follow the braided trail uphill through a gully that can hold snow until midsummer, watching for cairns, to a small tarn at the foot of the south ridge. Religion is on the main east face of the Notch Spire. Look for the leftmost of three prominent roofed dihedrals slightly left of center, where the first pitch begins with a leap across a moat from a huge flat flake.

review.notes: Route page: start and top-out on Notch Spire; descent from Spiral Route, AAI and trip page.

set.descent_text: From the notch, scramble south along a ledge to the small summit of the Notch Spire, which sits on the opposite side of the mountain from the climb. After descending the spire, work uphill north to find the West Gully, a third- to fourth-class talus gully, following cairns and a well-worn path. Several rap stations appear along the traverse, but cliffs lie below, so stay on the path; snow can remain in the upper gully until midsummer, and it is a poor place to be in an electrical storm. Descend the gully to the start of the route and retrace the approach past Lake Helene to Bear Lake. Three rappels with two 60 m ropes down the west face are the alternative.
set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the Fern Lake trail for roughly 3 miles to the saddle between Joe Mills Mountain and Notchtop. An unsigned but obvious trail on the left drops to Lake Helene. Circle the lake counterclockwise, then follow the braided trail uphill through a gully that can hold snow until midsummer, watching for cairns, to a small tarn at the foot of the south ridge. With the south ridge soaring above, cross the bottom of the tarn and go up to the left through mild talus and grass. After entering the gully, look for a ramp going up and right toward the ridge; an easy scramble leads to a perch on the crest, a good place to rope up.

review.notes: Route page: full approach and West Gully descent; trip page and AAI article agree on the West Gully and three-rappel alternative; NPS agrees on the trail distance.

set.descent_text: After about four pitches you reach the large East Meadows ledge, and a couple of hundred feet of the Spiral Route leads to the notch. From there, weave down the fourth-class northwest ridge, or make three double-rope rappels down the west face off two-bolt stations. To find the first rappel, scramble third class over the chimney and gully toward the west and look for a large boulder leaning against the wall. The West Gully is a further option back to the tarn. At the foot, retrace the approach past Lake Helene to Bear Lake.
set.approach: Start at the Bear Lake trailhead and follow the Fern Lake trail for roughly 3 miles to the saddle between Joe Mills Mountain and Notchtop. An unsigned but obvious trail on the left drops to Lake Helene. Circle the lake counterclockwise, then follow the braided trail uphill through a gully that can hold snow until midsummer, watching for cairns, to a small tarn at the foot of the south ridge. Topnotch is on the right side of the east face. Stand under that side of the face and look for the stellar plaque of rock about 80 feet tall, which is the crux pitch.

review.notes: Route page: East Meadows, notch, rappels and ridge descent; AAI article agrees on ridge and three double-rope rappels.
